title: Platform systems & services: Dashboards, Alerts, Runbooks, Roadmap & Retrospective — Q2 2026
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary:
This document consolidates the platform systems & services artifacts produced during Q2 2026: authoritative dashboards and alerting rules, primary runbooks for high-priority services, a short retrospective of ops incidents and mitigations, and the roadmap for the next two quarters. It is intended for the Platform, SRE, and Serving Runtime teams and any engineers who operate or build on top of Redwood’s platform runtime.

1) Purpose and scope
- Scope: global platform systems that support hosted API, Dedicated control plane, and Private deployments.
- Services covered: router-api, inference-gateway, kv-cache, batch-orchestrator, metrics-ingest, s3-proxy, auth-service.
- Audience: platform engineers, oncall rotations, incident commanders, product leads.

2) Ownership matrix (primary owners)
- router-api: Platform - owner: Priya Kapoor (platform-router)
- inference-gateway: Serving Runtime - owner: Liam Chen (runtime-gateway)
- kv-cache: Eng Platform - owner: Noah Rivera (cache-team)
- batch-orchestrator: Eng Infra - owner: Maya Singh (batch-scheduling)
- metrics-ingest: Observability - owner: Jordan Lee (metrics-team)
- auth-service: Security - owner: Sarah Patel (identity)

3) Dashboards and SLOs
- Central dashboard links (Grafana):
  - Platform Overview (grafana/internal/d/PLATFORM_OVERVIEW) — global traffic, p95/p99 latency, error-rate, capacity utilization.
  - Inference Gateway (grafana/internal/d/INFERENCE_GW) — per-model QPS, kv-cache hit-rate, GPU pool utilization.
  - Router API (grafana/internal/d/ROUTER_API) — request routing latency, 5xx rates, circuit-breaker counts.
  - Metrics & Logging (grafana/internal/d/OBSERVABILITY) — ingestion lag, retention, alert delivery success.

- SLOs (service-level commitments for platform teams):
  - Router API: 99.9% availability (30d window), p95 API latency <= 120ms
  - Inference Gateway: 99.5% availability (30d), median token latency per request <= 40ms
  - Metrics-ingest: 99% on-time ingestion (1h window)

- Key dashboard panels to inspect for triage (ordered):
  1. 5xx count and rate (router-api, inference-gateway)
  2. Request concurrency vs provisioned capacity (inference-gateway)
  3. KV cache hit-rate and eviction rate (kv-cache)
  4. GPU-driver errors and OOM events (GPU pool)
  5. Metrics ingestion lag and write errors (metrics-ingest)

4) Alerting (PagerDuty rules + thresholds)
- Alert naming convention: PLATFORM.<SERVICE>.<CONDITION>. Example: PLATFORM.INFERENCE_GW.HIGH_5XX
- Severity mapping: P0 (pager) / P1 (pager + slack) / P2 (slack) / P3 (ticket)

Representative alert rules (short-form):
- PLATFORM.ROUTER_API.HIGH_5XX — when 5xx rate > 1% over 5m AND total requests > 1000m -> P0
- PLATFORM.INFERENCE_GW.HIGH_LATENCY_P95 — p95 latency > 500ms for 10m -> P1
- PLATFORM.KV_CACHE.LOW_HIT_RATE — hit-rate < 60% for 15m -> P2 (investigate cache pressure / config)
- PLATFORM.METRICS.INGEST_LAG — ingestion lag > 5m for 10m -> P1
- PLATFORM.GPU.POOL_OOM — >3 OOM events in 5m across pool -> P0

Alert run cadence and responders:
- P0: immediate page to oncall + incident commander (IC) auto-assign.
- P1: page to oncall and product SLA slack channel.
- P2/P3: create ticket and notify owners via slack.

5) Runbooks (top-level, runbook snippets follow)
- Runbook structure for each service:
  - Symptoms: listed observables that indicate the incident class
  - Impact: service-level impact and customer-visible effects
  - Triage steps: checklist to collect data and isolate cause
  - Mitigation steps: short-lived fixes (scale/batch/reroute)
  - Postmortem checklist: collection of artifacts, timeline, RCA owners

Example: Inference Gateway High 5xx runbook (abbreviated)
1) Symptoms:
   - sudden spike in 5xx from inference-gateway, p95 token latency increased, downstream GPU OOMs logged
2) Impact:
   - failed generations for hosted customers and Dedicated traffic routed through affected pool
3) Triage steps (ordered):
   a) Check "Inference Gateway" Grafana: 5xx by error type and model
   b) Inspect GPU pool metrics for OOM and scheduling failures
   c) Query batch-orchestrator for recent job failures (kubectl logs / batch API)
   d) Check kv-cache eviction and hit-rate panels
4) Mitigation (fast):
   a) Scale up inference-gateway replicas by +30% (kubectl scale deployment inference-gateway --replicas=<N>)
   b) For GPU OOMs, rollback to previous quantization profile (if rollout active) or reduce batch-size via runtime feature flag
   c) Route a portion of traffic to fallback model variant (smart routing policy)
5) Post-incident steps:
   - Create incident ticket, capture timeline, assign RCA owner, schedule PM/eng review within 3 business days

6) Runbook: KV cache pressure (short)
1) Symptoms: cache hit-rate < 60%, eviction rate high, increased inference latency for repeated prompts
2) Quick triage: check cache size utilization, eviction policy, and per-tenant key counts
3) Mitigation: bump cache capacity for pool; enable prefix caching for affected routes; roll TTL changes if recent

7) Incident retrospective summary (Q2 2026 highlights)
- Summary of notable incidents (all items abbreviated):
  1) 2026-04-22: Inference Gateway transient OOM cascade — root cause: rollout of aggressive quantization+batching profile for a new model (impact: 2h partial degradation). Mitigation: automatic rollout holdback introduced; changed release gating.
  2) 2026-05-12: Metrics ingestion lag during region migration — root cause: incomplete backfill strategy; impact: delayed alerts and delayed SLO reporting for 6h. Mitigation: backfill tool + pre-migration dry-run checklist added.
  3) 2026-06-03: Router API spike due to client retry storm — root cause: client SDK retry bug + missing circuit-breaker tuning (impact: 45m elevated error rate). Mitigation: client SDK patch + tightened circuit breaker thresholds and default client retries reduced.

What went well:
- Faster oncall detection from improved dashboard panels (implemented in March) reduced mean time to detect by ~20%.
- New automatic holdback for quantization rollouts prevented a larger incident in May.

Action items (owners and timelines):
- Improve rollout gating for model performance changes: owner Liam Chen, due 2026-07-15
- Add end-to-end migration runbook for metrics with pre-migration dry-run steps: owner Jordan Lee, due 2026-07-01
- Create a client-SDK compatibility test harness that simulates retry storms: owner Priya Kapoor, due 2026-08-01

8) Roadmap (Q3–Q4 2026 priorities)
- Q3 2026 (primary):
  - Observability 2.0: trace-linked dashboards, distributed tail-sampling for large requests — owner: Jordan Lee — milestone: alpha by 2026-08-15
  - Runtime rollout safety: automated canary for quantization+batching, automatic rollback on OOM trends — owner: Liam Chen — milestone: beta by 2026-09-01
  - Cache autosizing: per-pool autoscaling of kv-cache based on workload patterns — owner: Noah Rivera — milestone: initial rollout 2026-09-15
- Q4 2026 (secondary):
  - Platform multi-region routing improvements (faster failover, capacity-aware routing) — owner: Priya Kapoor — milestone: design complete 2026-11-01
  - Billing/observability alignment: token-level cost attribution added to platform dashboards — owner: Finance-Infra PM (TBD) — milestone: pilot 2026-12-01

9) How-tos and common procedures (quick links)
- How to scale inference-gateway (runbook snippet):
  1. Confirm increased capacity in pool (check GPU pool autoscaler)
  2. kubectl scale deployment inference-gateway --replicas=<n>
  3. Monitor p95 latency and 5xx rate for 15 minutes

- How to add a Grafana panel for service 5xx counts:
  1. Open Grafana > Platform Overview dashboard > edit
  2. New panel: query: sum(rate(http_server_requests_total{job=~"router-api|inference-gateway",status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (job)
  3. Set panel thresholds, link to alert rule if necessary

10) Postmortem checklist (required after P0/P1):
- Timeline captured in the incident ticket
- All runbook steps and commands used documented
- Root cause and contributing factors identified
- Follow-up action owner and due date recorded
- Customer-facing summary drafted (if impacted)

Appendices
A) Sample alert rule (Prometheus-style, abbreviated):
- alert: PLATFORM_ROUTERAPI_HIGH_5XX
  expr: sum(rate(http_server_requests_total{job="router-api",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_server_requests_total{job="router-api"}[5m])) > 0.01
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "router-api 5xx rate > 1%"

B) Quick links
- Grafana: https://grafana.internal.redwood/platform
- PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.internal.redwood/org/platform
- Runbook directory (Confluence root): /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks

C) Notes and references

- SDK change: client-sdk/releases/v2.4.1 (retry fix)

Document maintenance

- Review cadence: quarterly review by reviewers listed above.
